SECURITY SEAL APPLICATION NOTES

Choosing the Right Container Seal for Your Shipment

Start with the closure, the identification you need and the checks made during each handover.

Define the application

Tell the supplier what you are sealing, how the locking point is arranged and the quantity required. A product name alone does not establish compatibility.

Confirm the identification

Discuss numbering and any marking requirements. Plan how the applied seal number will be recorded with the shipment documents and checked at each handover.

Confirm the supplied specification

Ask for the exact model, dimensions and removal method. If your operation requires a particular certification or transport standard, request supporting documentation for that model before ordering.

Prepare your enquiry

Include the application, approximate quantity, preferred marking and required timeline. Global Seals can help you discuss an appropriate sealing solution.

Product reference: Global Seals product information. Confirm the exact supplied model and your operating requirements with the team.

title: Inspecting a Seal at Destination: A Simple Checklist | Global Seals
description: Use seal inspection as part of your established receiving procedure before authorised removal.
body:
Home / Guides

SECURITY SEAL APPLICATION NOTES

Inspecting a Seal at Destination: A Simple Checklist

Use seal inspection as part of your established receiving procedure before authorised removal.

Check presence

Confirm that a seal is present at the intended locking point. Do not treat a seal alone as proof that the contents are unchanged.

Compare identification

Read the visible number and compare it with the shipment records. Record a missing or mismatched identifier rather than assuming it is correct.

Inspect condition

Look for visible damage or signs of interference around the seal and locking point. Follow your organisation's escalation procedure if something does not match expectations.

Record before removal

Record the inspection result according to your receiving procedure. Only authorised personnel should remove the seal using the appropriate method for the supplied model.

SECURITY SEAL APPLICATION NOTES

Meter Seals: Where They Fit in Routine Utility Checks

A suitable seal gives a clear reference when checking access to meter enclosures and related equipment.

Identify the sealing points

Describe the enclosure and the points the seal or wire must pass through. Share dimensions when requesting product guidance.

Discuss the locking format

Meter, roto and other wire seals use different closure arrangements. Ask which supplied model suits your application and access requirements.

Plan routine checks

Include seal presence, identification and visible condition in your established inspection procedure. A seal supports these checks rather than replacing them.

Check compatibility before ordering

For wire-based closures, confirm the compatible wire specification and length. Ask about marking options for the exact model.

Home / Guides

SECURITY SEAL APPLICATION NOTES

Numbering, Logos and Barcodes: Marking Options Explained

Marking helps your team connect a physical seal to the records used in daily operations.

Serial identification

A visible identifier can be recorded at application and compared at handover. Confirm the numbering format and whether it suits your record system.

Logos and text

Tell the supplier what identification you would like printed or marked. Available space and marking options depend on the model; request confirmation rather than assuming every product offers the same choices.

Barcode requirements

If you need a barcode, explain the intended scanning workflow and format. Confirm availability and suitability on the exact supplied seal.

Approve the details

Include quantities and marking requirements in your enquiry. Confirm the final specification and any artwork before placing an order.
